summary.text: The Achaemenid Empire was an ancient Iranian empire founded by Cyrus the Great in 550 BC and based on the Iranian plateau.
At its peak it covered roughly 5.5 million square kilometres, the largest empire of its time, stretching from the Balkans in the west to the Indus Valley in the east.
Alexander the Great conquered it entirely in 330 BC, and most of its lands then came under the Seleucid Empire and the Ptolemaic Kingdom.

facts.label: Peak size
facts.value: About 5.5 million square kilometres, largest of its time

facts.label: Home region
facts.value: Persis, in the southwestern Iranian plateau

facts.label: Named after
facts.value: Achaemenes, credited as the dynasty's progenitor

items.prompt: Cyrus rose from Persis and built an empire by conquest. Which three states did he defeat?
items.explain: From Persis, Cyrus defeated Media, Lydia and the Neo-Babylonian Empire.

items.prompt: Cyrus took over the Median empire. What else did he end up inheriting?

options.label: Its territorial conflicts with Lydia and Babylon
Its alliance with Lydia against Babylon

items.explain: By inheriting Astyages' empire, he also inherited the territorial conflicts the Medes had with Lydia and the Neo-Babylonian Empire.

items.prompt: The empire expanded rapidly, yet some campaigns failed. Where were its armies repulsed?
items.explain: The empire was repulsed from Scythia in 513 BC and from Greece in 492 to 490 and 480 to 479 BC.

items.prompt: After Alexander the Great died, who took over most of the old Persian lands?

options.label: The Seleucid Empire and the Ptolemaic Kingdom
Cyrus's descendants, restored to the throne

items.explain: After Alexander's death most of the former territories came under the Seleucid Empire and the Ptolemaic Kingdom; the Parthians took power almost a century later.

items.prompt: Before building an empire, how did the Persians live?

options.label: As nomadic herders on the western Iranian Plateau
As settled traders along the coast
As soldiers serving the Median king

items.explain: The Achaemenid Empire was founded by nomadic Persians, originally nomadic pastoralists in the western Iranian Plateau.

items.prompt: After taking Babylon, Cyrus claimed that the previous king had upset the proper worship. What was he presenting himself as doing?

options.label: Founding the cult of a new god

items.explain: Cyrus portrayed himself as restoring the divine order disrupted by Nabonidus, who had promoted the cult of Sin rather than Marduk.
